present_simple: She ___ to work by train every day.
They ___ enough time to finish the task.
The museum ___ at nine every morning.
Third-person singular takes -s in the present simple.
past_simple: Finished past actions normally use the past simple.
Use the past form went for a completed past event.
present_perfect: Present perfect links a past action to the present experience.
Use has lived with since for a continuing situation.
future: By next June, they ___ the project.
Future perfect describes an action completed before a future point.
conditionals: If I ___ more time, I would join the course.
Second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause.
modals: You ___ wear a helmet when riding this bike.
articles: She bought ___ umbrella because it was raining.
Use an before a vowel sound in umbrella.
prepositions: Use on with days and dates.
gerunds: Enjoy is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
passive: Past passive uses was/were + past participle.
reported: Reported speech commonly backshifts present to past after a past reporting verb.
relatives: The book ___ I borrowed was excellent.
That can introduce a defining relative clause for a thing.
inversion: Hardly ___ the train when it began to rain.
Negative adverbial inversion places the auxiliary before the subject.
advanced_modals: He ___ have forgotten the appointment; he never arrived.
Must have + past participle expresses a strong deduction about the past.
parallelism: The course aims to improve writing, speaking, and ___.
Items in a series should use parallel grammatical forms.
